newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila 9-mth refined sugar imports at $60 mln.
newsitem.headline: Manila 9-mth refined sugar imports at $60 mln.

text.p: The Philippines imported $60 million worth of refined sugar, mostly from Thailand, from January to September this year, according to the Department of Trade and Industry.
Documents issued by the state agency said the country's imports from neigbouring Southeast Asian countries reached $44 million.
"More than 90 percent of our sugar imports from ASEAN comes from Thailand," it said.
It also said that refined sugar imports last year grew by 393 percent to $52.7 million from $10.7 million in 1994.

The Philippine Sugar Millers Association (PSMA) had asked the government to withdraw the 35 percent rebate on duties on the import of refined sugar from member-nations of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

"We are the only country in the ASEAN Free Trade Area and the world that gives incentives or encourages the importation of refined sugar over raws in spite of the fact that even the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and the World Trade Organisation recognise sugar as a sensitive agricultural product," the PSMA said in a letter submitted to the Tariff Commission.
The PSMA said the over-imports of refined sugar resulted in the drop of the prevailing price of local raws by at least 20 percent.

The trade department said it will coordinate with the Tariff Commission and the Bureau of Customs to determine whether the duty-free imports of refined sugar in the country's so-called "economic zones," might have exacerbated the situation.
